alibi_default.s: Home, in bed, like every night. Nobody to vouch for me but the cat.
I had the television on until the news, then I was out. Ask the neighbours if my light went off, they notice such things.
Sound asleep, Detective. I have a bad back and an early start, and I'm in bed by nine like a Christian.
At home. I was reading until my eyes gave up. You can check the library card if you think a book can alibi me.
Dead to the world. I wasn't in a state to be anywhere else. I'd been on my feet since five.
Where I always am. Home, then bed, then the bus. I know that isn't exciting, but it's true.
Home. I don't go out after dark if I can help it. Not in this town. Not lately.
Out for a smoke on the step about ten, then bed. Nothing happened. If it had, I'd have gone looking.
I was doing my accounts at the kitchen table until midnight and I can show you the pencil marks. That's the exciting life of a person who counts every dollar.
I was home. My mum rang about half ten, if it helps, and we talked about nothing for an hour.
Home, with the radio. I had it on low. The radio is good company, and it never asks where you've been.
Home. Asleep on the sofa with my boots on, if I'm honest. I only woke because the dog wanted out.
I was in. I did my rounds of the house, locked up, and I said my prayers. I always do.
At home, flat out. Something about this town makes you tired at that hour. It's the damp, I think. Or the lake.
In bed. Ask my neighbour, who complains if I so much as flush after eleven.

saw_none.s: Asleep by ten. I didn't see or hear a thing.
I'd like to help. But I had my curtains drawn and a pillow over my head. There's a draught in my bedroom window that whistles.
No. And I'd tell you if I had, truly. I'm not one to keep a thing like that in.
I saw nothing. Honestly, nothing. You'd be surprised how little you see in this town when the fog comes down.
Nothing at all. If I'd seen something I'd be in the Sheriff's office right now with my hat in my hand.
I don't look out at night. Not anymore. You see things you don't need to know about.
I was working. If anything went by, it went by without me.
Not a thing. I heard the lake, but then I always hear the lake.
Nobody asked me that last time, either. No. No, there was nothing to see.
I was on the phone most of the evening. My sister does go on. If a brass band had passed I'd have missed it.
I couldn't say. My eyes aren't what they were and the street lamps on this road have been out for a month.
I wish I had. It'd be a relief to be useful. But no. I had the early shift and I slept like a stone.

suspects_none.s: I wouldn't like to say. Everyone liked {v}, mostly.
I don't gossip, Detective. If I'd a name, I'd give it you. I haven't.
{v}? Everybody had a word to say about {v}, and none of it was that.
You'll have to ask someone who pays more attention than I do.
It's not my place to point. That's how this town got into the state it's in.
If I said a name, and I was wrong, I'd have to live next to them. No.
Plenty of folk had a bone to pick with {v}. Not enough of them had the stomach.
Whoever it was, they knew {v}. That's all I'd swear to.
Honestly? I haven't the faintest. And I've lain awake half the night looking for one.
Nobody I could name without being sorry later.

alibi_unknown.s: I couldn't tell you where {about} was. Not my business.
{about}? I've no idea. We're not close enough for me to know their nights.
I'd be guessing, and I won't guess about a person's whereabouts. Not to a detective.
No notion. Ask {about}, why don't you. People answer to their own names more honestly than to other people's.
Last I saw {about}, it was the afternoon, and they looked fine. After that, who knows.
I mind my own street, Detective. {about} lives on someone else's.
I don't keep a diary of other folks' evenings. Though I know some who do.
I'd rather not say something about {about} that I can't stand behind.

repeat.s: You've asked me that already. The answer hasn't changed.
We've been over this. I haven't remembered anything new, I promise.
Same as before. Asking again won't make it different. Believe me, I've tried.
Detective, I told you. Are you doubting me, or just testing my patience?
Please. I'm trying to be helpful. But I've said it, and I don't have more.
You asked that. I said what I said. There isn't a second answer hiding behind the first.
Dear, you've asked that one. Come in and have a cup of tea and ask me something else.
Haven't we done this? I'm not being rude, I just don't want to say it differently by mistake.
I've answered that once and I'm not going to improve on it. Ask me something I haven't said.

present_unknown.s: I don't know what you want me to say about that.
I've never seen it. If it's a clue, I'm sorry, it's not one I can read.
Is that supposed to mean something to me? Because it doesn't.
No. No, that's nothing to do with me. I'd tell you.
I couldn't say. It's not the sort of thing I'd have noticed.
I'm sorry. That's a mystery to me, and I don't like mysteries. They have a way of coming to the door.
Is this a test? You'll have to be plainer than that.

claim_killer.s: I was in bed by ten. Alone, before you ask. I didn't hear a thing.
At home. I keep regular hours, Detective, and I'll tell you anyone in the street will say the same. My light went out at ten.
I was in the house all evening. I didn't see anyone and no one saw me. It's the quiet life I've chosen.
Home. I'd had a long day. If you're asking whether I went out, I didn't. I wouldn't have the energy for it.
In bed. Reading, then out. I don't need you to believe me. I need you to find the person who did it.
I was home. I know how it looks that I can't prove it. I don't ask for sympathy. Only for fairness.
Home, locked up and asleep. It's a terrible thing, what's happened. Terrible. I can't stop thinking about it.
Asleep. I took a tablet for the headache and I didn't wake until the cat sat on my chest.
At home with the lights off. I'll be frank, Detective: I wasn't fond of {v}, and I'm not going to pretend. I also didn't kill them.
I stayed in. People are making a lot of what they think I was up to. I was up to nothing.

claim_secret.s: I was home asleep. Nothing to tell. I'm not hiding anything.
At home. In bed. I don't see why you're looking at me like that.
Home. All night. And I'd thank you not to ask twice.
I was in. Honestly. Ask... no, there's nobody to ask. I was in.
At home, alone, on my own sofa. I don't know what else you want from me.
I stayed in. It was raining, or it should have been. I stayed in, that's all.
Bed. By eleven. I can't help it if nobody saw me go up.

claim_weak.s: I was at home. On my own. I know how that sounds.
I went home after work and I stayed there. There's no one to say so but me, and I understand that isn't much.
Home, no company, no alibi, and no reason to need one. Go on, write it down.
I was home. Please believe me. I'm not good at this. I've never been questioned by anyone in my life.
At home with a tin of soup and the radio. I could tell you the programmes, if that helps.
Home. The pub was too loud and I didn't feel like talking. So there you are: unsociable, but innocent.

claim_verified.s: I was {where}, all night. Ask anyone there.
{where}, from eight until the small hours. There's a dozen people who'll say so, and half of them don't like me.
You can ask them. I was {where}, and I'd be offended if you didn't.
I was {where}. I stayed late because I couldn't face going home. I'm glad of it now.
{where}. The whole night, Detective. I was never alone for five minutes.
I was {where}, and that's where they'll tell you I was. I didn't know I needed a witness. I do now.

victim_close.s: One of the best. I can't believe it.
{v} was my... they were everything to this street. I don't know who we are without them.
We were close. Closer than I'd ever tell anyone who wasn't a detective.
I keep thinking they'll walk through the door. I keep putting out two cups.
They'd have given you the coat off their back. And you tell me somebody did this? I won't have it. I won't.
I was going to see them tomorrow. We had plans. It was only a sandwich, but it was the plan.

victim_friend.s: A good neighbour. A good person.
{v}? Lovely. Never a cross word. Which is why, I suppose, there has to be something wrong with it.
We got along. Not best friends, but friends. I'd have said hello to them every day of my life.
Friendly. Fair. Not one to make a fuss. I'd have called them a rock.
Decent. That word does a lot of work in this town, and in their case it was true.
{v} was good to me when I wasn't good to anybody. I'll say that.

victim_acq.s: I knew them to nod to. Kept themselves to themselves.
We said good morning. We said good evening. In this town that's a friendship of a sort.
Polite. Quiet. The kind of person you only notice when they're not there.
Not well. Well enough to know they weren't unhappy, until lately. They'd gone quiet.
I saw them at the shop most weeks. They always counted their change twice.

victim_stranger.s: I couldn't tell you a thing about them. I knew the name and I knew the house. That's all, honestly.
To me they were a nod across the road and a coat on the peg. Make of that what you will.
We'd never really spoken. It's a small town, but not as small as people say.

victim_bad.s: We didn't get on, I won't lie. I wouldn't wish this on them.
We'd words. More than once. I'll own that. I didn't hate them. I just didn't like being in a room with them.
Everyone knows we'd fallen out. It doesn't make me glad. It makes me the first person you ask. I understand.
They'd a way of looking at you that made you feel like a debt. But I'm sorry they're gone.

victim_enemy.s: I won't pretend to be sorry. But I didn't do it.
You want me to say I'm sorry? I'm sorry it's you asking. I'm not sorry they're gone. But I didn't do it.
We hated each other. Everyone knew. That's why it'd be stupid of me. I'm not stupid.
God forgive me, a part of me is glad. A larger part of me is terrified of you. I had nothing to do with it.

cover_good_person.s: They're a good person. Whatever you've heard, you've heard it wrong.
You don't know them like I do. Whatever it looks like, you're wrong, and you'll see that.
I've known them my whole life. They haven't got it in them. Please. Look elsewhere.
They'd never. They get upset if they step on a snail. I'm telling you this as someone who loves them.

rapport_refuse.s: {n} glances away. "I don't know you well enough for that."
{n} shakes their head. "Not to a stranger with a notebook. Come back when you've earned it."
{n} lowers their voice and then doesn't use it. "No. I can't. Not yet."
{n} gives you a long look. "You haven't sat at my table. I don't tell the people who haven't sat at my table."

pressure_quiet.s: {n} goes quiet. They know something, and you have nothing to put in front of them yet.
{n}'s eyes flick to the door and back. There is something there. You haven't got the lever to move it.
{n} presses their lips together. The silence has weight. Whatever it is, they're keeping it from you, and the notebook is not yet thick enough to take it.

refuse_damaged.s: {n} stands with the door open six inches. "After what you said about me in front of the whole street? No." The door closes.
{n} won't look at you. "You had your say. The whole town heard it. I've nothing to tell you."
{n} is in the doorway with their coat on, as if leaving. "I'm going to my sister's. Don't follow me."
{n} says nothing. They put one hand flat on the door, as though to hold it up, and then the door is shut.

cold_forgot.s: I... it's been so long. Was it the Tuesday? I really couldn't tell you now. It's all gone soft.
I thought I'd remember. I told myself I would. And now it's as if I'd dreamed it.
Detective, a week? You expect me to remember minutes? I can barely remember what I had for breakfast.
It was something. I know it was something. Whatever it was, it's gone, and I am sorry.
